translation: Having obtained this rubbing method, one can not only govern one's own existing disease, but also treat disease that has not yet arisen. Is this not what the 《Suwen》 means by saying that the perfected person treats disease before it arises and does not treat disease that has already arisen? If one says to people, “I cannot,” this is not doing it, not being unable. To be content that one's own body cannot dwell in benevolence and follow righteousness is called self-abandonment. Is it a pity? Or not? Mencius says: For the tung and catalpa trees of a hand-span, if people want them to live, they all know how to nourish them; how could one love one's body less than the tung and catalpa trees? Even if there is no all-day laborer, one can still steal half a day of leisure wherever one is.
